completion_data.completion_summary: Implemented the books extension's first PreToolUse Write|Edit hook, blocking any modification or deletion of a committed line in books/book-convention-evidence/NN-*.md while permitting pure appends; built its 29-assertion forgery-probed fixture suite, wired manifest.json and a new bare settings fragment, and verified the deploy against the live consumer repository (registration bare, joined to the existing matcher block, idempotent, and firing correctly against a real evidence file).

memory_candidates.content: For a write-time PreToolUse guard enforcing 'append-only relative to git HEAD, free edits past that point', split the comparison into three values rather than one baseline: FLOOR (git show HEAD:<path>, the immutable floor), DISK (current on-disk content), and TAIL (DISK with the FLOOR prefix sliced off via ${DISK:${#FLOOR}}, bash substring-by-length, never a glob-based strip). Write-tool checks need only FLOOR-is-prefix-of-new-content. Edit-tool checks need TWO independent allow patterns: (a) old_string is a suffix of DISK and new_string begins with old_string (a pure append), or (b) old_string is a suffix of TAIL alone (a free edit confined to the uncommitted region, which by construction can never reach the floor). A single-pattern design using only 'old_string suffix of the HEAD baseline' looks sufficient but incorrectly refuses a legitimate in-place correction to an uncommitted trailing entry, since that text never appears in the HEAD baseline at all -- this gap only surfaces when a fixture specifically tests an in-place (non-append) edit to the uncommitted tail, not just append-style edits.

For a books-extension-style forgery probe against a shell script predicate (not a Lean/lake predicate), copy the real script into the test workdir, apply exactly ONE targeted sed substitution to disable or neutralize a single predicate (e.g. the terminal 'exit 2' line, a scope-match case arm, or a specific command-substitution baseline lookup), assert via `cmp -s` that the substitution actually changed the copy (so a probe can't silently pass by failing to stub anything), then drive the stubbed copy with the SAME payload a real behavioral case used and assert the real case's expectation now breaks (probe_expect_broken: actual != real). Always pair a refusal-predicate probe with a scope/admit-predicate probe (the admit half): a refusal-only probe suite cannot distinguish a correct refusal from a predicate that refuses everything.

When constructing a 'jq missing from PATH' fail-open fixture for a hook script, do not set PATH to a nonexistent/empty directory -- the hook's own location-resolution preamble (e.g. `dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"`) needs basic coreutils and will crash before the intended guard ever runs. Instead, compute a coreutils-only PATH via `dirname "$(command -v cat)"` (or similar) that excludes only the directory containing the target dependency, with a graceful INFO-skip guard if the environment happens to co-locate that dependency with coreutils anyway (e.g. `PATH="$COREUTILS_DIR" command -v jq` still succeeds).
